previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with severe diastolic heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, atrial fibrillation, and a PleurX catheter for recurrent pleural effusions was admitted for generalized weakness and a reported tremor. He had recently been hospitalized for heart failure and pneumonia. Workup revealed worsening right pleural effusion and signs of infection. He was started on vancomycin and cefepime for suspected healthcare-associated pneumonia with empyema. Due to poor drainage, tPA was instilled through the PleurX catheter after reversing anticoagulation. The next day, he developed hemothorax, hypotension, and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate, requiring ICU admission, blood transfusions, and pressor support. The hemothorax resolved with drainage, and he was stabilized. Pleural fluid cultures confirmed MRSA, and he completed a course of vancomycin. His heart rhythm was controlled with amiodarone and adjusted metoprolol. He was transitioned to oral diuretics, warfarin was restarted at a reduced dose, and he was discharged home with home health for antibiotic infusions and follow-up.

his uremia resolved, pt. had noted to have return to his 
baseline neurologic status.

ongoing diuresis as stated above.  ___ resolved with return to
